    Nested Regions and Sites: Exact Balanced Mixed Inference

    nested-regions-sites.Rmd

    This vignette demonstrates exact fixed-effect tests at three levels of a nested design. A restoration treatment is assigned to regions, a substrate treatment is assigned to sites within regions, and a microhabitat treatment is assigned to replicate quadrats within sites. Every region has the same number of sites and every site has the same number of quadrats.

    The example is simulated because the standard vegan community datasets do not encode a complete balanced region/site experiment. The Bray–Curtis workflow is the same as in the dune and pyrifos vignettes.

    Simulate a balanced ecological community 

    sampling <- expand.grid(
  quadrat = factor(1:3),
  site = factor(1:2),
  region = factor(1:8)
)
sampling$treatment <- factor(
  ifelse(as.integer(sampling$region) <= 4, "reference", "restored")
)
sampling$substrate <- factor(
  ifelse(sampling$site == "1", "natural", "enhanced")
)
sampling$microhabitat <- sampling$quadrat

set.seed(20260718)
species <- 12
nested_site <- interaction(sampling$region, sampling$site, drop = TRUE)
baseline <- log(seq(2.5, 7, length.out = species))
region_shift <- c(rep(0.3, species / 2), rep(-0.15, species / 2))
site_shift <- c(rep(-0.1, species / 2), rep(0.2, species / 2))
quadrat_shift <- rbind(
  rep(-0.08, species), rep(0, species), rep(0.08, species)
)
region_effect <- matrix(rnorm(8 * species, sd = 0.25), 8, species)
site_effect <- matrix(rnorm(16 * species, sd = 0.18), 16, species)

linear_predictor <- matrix(baseline, nrow(sampling), species, byrow = TRUE) +
  region_effect[sampling$region, ] + site_effect[nested_site, ] +
  outer(as.numeric(sampling$treatment == "restored"), region_shift) +
  outer(as.numeric(sampling$substrate == "enhanced"), site_shift) +
  quadrat_shift[sampling$microhabitat, ]
community <- matrix(
  rpois(length(linear_predictor), lambda = exp(linear_predictor)),
  nrow(sampling), species
)
colnames(community) <- paste0("taxon", seq_len(species))
table(sampling$region, sampling$site)
#>    
#>     1 2
#>   1 3 3
#>   2 3 3
#>   3 3 3
#>   4 3 3
#>   5 3 3
#>   6 3 3
#>   7 3 3
#>   8 3 3

    Compile first, then derive the test

    The slash is structural: it creates region and region:site random intercepts and records containment provenance in the Design Object.

    bray <- vegan::vegdist(community, method = "bray")
design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + substrate + microhabitat + (1 | region/site),
  data = sampling,
  distance = bray
)
design$random_term_table
#>          term  origin parent   variables  expression slope correlated
#> 1      region    main   <NA>      region      region  <NA>      FALSE
#> 2 region:site nesting region region:site region/site  <NA>      FALSE

    Each numerator has the same null EMS as the residual part of its assigned stratum. With two sites and three quadrats per site, a region-level numerator contains one residual unit, three site-within-region units, and six region units. A site-level numerator contains the first two components, while an observation-level numerator contains residual variation only.

    ems <- derive_nested_ems(design)
lapply(ems, function(term) {
  term[c("assignment_level", "parent_level", "numerator_under_null",
         "denominator_term")]
})
#> $treatment
#> $treatment$assignment_level
#> [1] "region"
#> 
#> $treatment$parent_level
#> [1] "grand mean"
#> 
#> $treatment$numerator_under_null
#>    residual      region region:site 
#>           1           6           3 
#> 
#> $treatment$denominator_term
#> [1] "region within fixed model"

#> 
#> $substrate
#> $substrate$assignment_level

#> 
#> $substrate$parent_level
#> [1] "region"

#> $substrate$numerator_under_null

#> 1.000000e+00 6.314393e-16 3.000000e+00 
#>

    Test every term at its assignment level

    The permutation operates on fitted-model residuals. For restoration, each region’s complete descendant hierarchy moves intact. Substrate permutes intact sites within each region, and microhabitat permutes quadrats within each site. This vignette draws a small Monte Carlo sample from each level-specific space.

    fit <- permanova_nested(
  design,
  permutations = 99,
  seed = 20260718,
  truncate = TRUE
)
fit$table
#>                                        term df         ss         ms
#> 1                                 treatment  1 0.27964223 0.27964223
#> 2                                 substrate  1 0.11831354 0.11831354

    Unrestricted variance components are the primary estimates. A negative value is retained because sampling variation can place a method-of-moments estimate below zero. The truncated vector is a separate sensitivity result.

    fit$variance_components$unrestricted
#>    residual      region region:site 
#> 0.025746729 0.004703338 0.006163359
fit$variance_components$truncated
#>    residual      region region:site 
#> 0.025746729 0.004703338 0.006163359

    Cross-level interactions need orthogonal contrasts

    The ordinary split-plot formula is safe, but R’s default treatment contrasts do not generally make a main-effect projector orthogonal to its interaction. The engine therefore rejects that parameterization instead of silently assigning the main effect to the wrong hierarchy level. Assign sum-to-zero contrasts explicitly for balanced crossed factors:

    default_crossed <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment * substrate + (1 | region/site), sampling, bray
)
conditionMessage(tryCatch(
  permanova_nested(default_crossed, permutations = 0),
  error = identity
))
#> [1] "Fixed term `treatment` spans multiple hierarchy levels or is not orthogonal to its parent stratum; use a level-specific, within-parent-balanced parameterization. For balanced cross-level factor interactions, assign explicit orthogonal contrasts such as `contr.sum` to the crossed factors before compiling the design."

orthogonal_sampling <- sampling
contrasts(orthogonal_sampling$treatment) <- contr.sum(2)
contrasts(orthogonal_sampling$substrate) <- contr.sum(2)
orthogonal_crossed <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment * substrate + (1 | region/site),
  orthogonal_sampling,
  bray
)
permanova_nested(
  orthogonal_crossed,
  permutations = 0
)$assignment_levels
#>           treatment           substrate treatment:substrate 
#>            "region"       "region:site"       "region:site"

    Contrasts are not changed automatically: doing so could change the hypothesis represented by a user’s formula. The explicit assignment above is local to the copied factors and leaves session-wide contrast options untouched.

    Know the boundary

    A raw gradient can contain both differences among regions and differences among quadrats. That is not one level-specific hypothesis, so the nested engine rejects it rather than choosing a denominator silently.

    sampling$ambiguous_gradient <-
  as.numeric(sampling$region) + as.numeric(sampling$quadrat)
ambiguous <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ ambiguous_gradient + (1 | region/site), sampling, bray
)
conditionMessage(tryCatch(
  permanova_nested(ambiguous, permutations = 0),
  error = identity
))
#> [1] "Fixed term `ambiguous_gradient` spans multiple hierarchy levels or is not orthogonal to its parent stratum; use a level-specific, within-parent-balanced parameterization. For balanced cross-level factor interactions, assign explicit orthogonal contrasts such as `contr.sum` to the crossed factors before compiling the design."

    Decompose such a gradient into explicit between-region and within-site predictors before testing. Balanced cross-level factor interactions are also supported when explicit orthogonal contrasts such as contr.sum make their estimable projector belong to one stratum. The same explicit rejection still applies to unequal replication, incomplete hierarchies, crossed random terms, random slopes, and multiple independent nesting trees. Those are future engines, not hidden approximations.
